Re: Protest of Proposed 765 kV Transmission Line Project
Applicant: Oncor Electric Delivery Company / Lower Colorado River Authority
Docket No.: 59475

To the Public Utility Commission of Texas:

1 submit this formal protest regarding the proposed 765 kV transmission line
project that would impact Concho and McCulloch Counties, Texas.

As a person that frequents this area for agritourism purposes, !| am directly
affected by the proposed routing of this project. The intrusion of this transmission
line would limit my ability to pursue activities on the affected properties. This will
also have a negative economic impact on surrounding towns and businesses as |
would have to take my business elsewhere.

LEGAL BASIS FOR PROTEST

1. Failure to Satisfy Certificate of Convenience and Necessity (CCN)
Requirements

Under Texas Utilities Code §37.051-§37.056, a utility must obtain or amend a
Certificate of Convenience and Necessity (CCN) prior to constructing a
transmission line.

The Commission is required to evaluate:
e Need for service
« Adequacy of existing infrastructure
¢ Community values and environmental integrity
« Use of existing rights-of-way
« Alignment with property boundaries and land use

There is insufficient evidence that this project meets these statutory criteria,
particularly with respect to:

¢ Use of existing corridors

« Minimization of impacts to rural landowners

 * Demonstrated necessity versus alternatives
2. Violation of PUC Routing Criteria (Substantive Rule §25.101)
The Commission must evaluate routing based on:

¢ Prudent avoidance of EMF exposure

* Community, aesthetic, and environmental impacts

« Use of compatible rights-of-way

The proposed route through Concho and McCulloch Counties appears inconsistent
with these requirements by:

¢ Introducing new corridors rather than co-locating infrastructure

« Creating disproportionate burdens on rural landowners

¢ Failing to adequately mitigate visual and environmental harm
3. Property Rights and Eminent Domain Concerns

Texas law grants utilities eminent domain authority to acquire easements if
negotiations fail.

However, this authority is contingent upon lawful CCN approval and proper route
selection. The proposed routing:

* Imposes long-term restrictions on agricultural land use

» Reduces property values

* Creates permanent encumbrances on private land
4. Failure to Adequately Consider Environmental and Agricultural Impacts
PUC rules require consideration of environmental integrity and land use impacts.
In Concho and McCulloch Counties, this includes:

+ Disruption to ranching, farming, and agritourism operations

¢ Soil erosion risks in fragile rangeland

¢ Wildlife habitat fragmentation
5. Inadequate Public Participation and Rural Impact Equity

The routing process must incorporate meaningful landowner input and equitable
burden distribution.

 Concho and McCulloch County landowners appear to bear disproportionate impacts
relative to urban beneficiaries.

REQUEST FOR RELIEF
| respectfully request that the Commission:

1. Deny the proposed routing through Concho and McCulloch Counties.

N

. Require full evaluation of co-location alternatives along existing corridors.
3. Mandate a comprehensive Environmental Impact Assessment.

4. Require demonstration of necessity under §37.056.

5. Ensure compliance with prudent avoidance standards.

Respectfully submitted,
[Your Signature]

 Judge and Commissioners,

My name is [Your Name], and | ama frequent visitor to Concho, Menard and
McCulloch Counties, Texas. | would like to express my opposition to the
proposed 765 kV transmission line project being developed by Oncor Electric
Delivery Company and the Lower Colorado River Authority.

This project represents a major and permanent change to these counties.
While | understand the importance of reliable electricity infrastructure, this
proposal raises serious concerns for the area.

First, it threatens private property rights. Many landowners in these counties
could be subject to eminent domain, which would permanently impact their
land, livelihoods, and property values.

Second, the environmental and agricultural impacts are significant. These
large transmission corridors can disrupt farming, ranching and agritourism
operations, fragment wildlife habitats, and affect soil and water resources.

Third, the visual impact of 765 kV transmission lines will fundamentally
change the rural character of these counties. This is not a temporary
disruption—this is a permanent industrialization of the landscape.

Finally, many residents and Property users are concerned about potential
health and safety impacts associated with being near high-voltage
transmission lines.

| respectfully ask this Court to:
* Formally oppose the proposed routing through these counties;
* Advocate for affected landowners, residents, and agritourism entities;

¢ Request additional studies and public input before any decisions are
made;

¢ Work with state regulators, including the Public Utility Commission of
Texas, to ensure concerns are heard.

These counties should not bear a disproportionate burden for infrastructure
that primarily serves broader regional interests.

Thank you for your time and for representing the people that reside in, and
travel to, these counties for recreation.

anny johnc —_ S-/%- 27

Respectfully,

Re: Protest of Proposed 765 kV Transmission Line Project
Applicant: Oncor Electric Delivery Company / Lower Colorado River Authority
Docket No.: 59475
To the Public Utility Commission of Texas:
I submit this formal protest regarding the proposed 765 kV transmission line
project that would impact Concho and McCulloch Counties, Texas.
As a person that frequents this area for agritourism purposes, I am directly
affected by the proposed routing of this project. The intrusion of this transmission
line would limit my ability to pursue activities on the affected properties. This will
also have a negative economic impact on surrounding towns and businesses as I
would have to take my business elsewhere.
LEGAL BASIS FOR PROTEST
1. Failure to Satisfy Certificate of Convenience and Necessity (CCN)
Requirements
Under Texas Utilities Code §37.051-§37.056, a utility must obtain or amend a
Certificate of Convenience and Necessity (CCN) prior to constructing a
transmission line.
The Commission is required to evaluate:
   ·   Need for service
   ·   Adequacy of existing infrastructure
   •   Community values and environmental integrity
   ·   Use of existing rights-of-way
   •   Alignment with property boundaries and land use
There is insufficient evidence that this project meets these statutory criteria,
particularly with respect to:
   ·   Use of existing corridors
   ·   Minimization of impacts to rural landowners
    ·   Demonstrated necessity versus alternatives
2. Violation of PUC Routing Criteria (Substantive Rule §25.101)
The Commission must evaluate routing based on:
   ·   Prudent avoidance of EMF exposure
   ·   Community, aesthetic, and environmental impacts
   ·   Use of compatible rights-of-way
The proposed route through Concho and McCulloch Counties appears inconsistent
with these requirements by:
   •   Introducing new corridors rather than co-locating infrastructure
   ·   Creating disproportionate burdens on rural landowners
   ·   Failing to adequately mitigate visual and environmental harm
3. Property Rights and Eminent Domain Concerns
Texas law grants utilities eminent domain authority to acquire easements if
negotiations fail.
However, this authority is contingent upon lawful CCN approval and proper route
selection. The proposed routing:
   ·   Imposes long-term restrictions on agricultural land use
   ·   Reduces property values
   •   Creates permanent encumbrances on private land
4. Failure to Adequately Consider Environmental and Agricultural Impacts
PUC rules require consideration of environmental integrity and land use impacts.
In Concho and McCulloch Counties, this includes:
   •   Disruption to ranching, farming, and agritourism operations
   ·   Soil erosion risks in fragile rangeland
   ·   Wildlife habitat fragmentation
5. Inadequate Public Participation and Rural Impact Equity
The routing process must incorporate meaningful Iandowner input and equitable
burden distribution.
 Concho and McCulloch County landowners appear to bear disproportionate impacts
relative to urban beneficiaries.
REQUEST FOR RELIEF
I respectfully request that the Commission:
   1. Deny the proposed routing through Concho and McCulloch Counties.
   2. Require full evaluation of co-location alternatives along existing corridors.
   3. Mandate a comprehensive Environmental Impact Assessment.
  4. Require demonstration of necessity under §37.056.

   5. Ensure compliance with prudent avoidance standards.
Respectfully submitted,
[Your Signature]
